editorial_intro: Rajkumar Hirani's OTT debut arrives alongside Enola Holmes 3, Silo's perfect-score return, and a stacked week of Indian originals across Telugu, Malayalam, and Hindi.

picks.title: Pritam and Pedro
picks.synopsis: Rajkumar Hirani's OTT debut pairs Arshad Warsi as an old-school Goa cop with Vir Hirani as a young hacker, forced together when a minister's son is kidnapped by a dangerous cybercriminal played by Vikrant Massey. Boman Irani and Mona Singh round out the ensemble.
picks.why_watch: Arshad Warsi reunites with Rajkumar Hirani for the first time since Munna Bhai — that alone is worth tuning in.

picks.title: Tavvai
picks.synopsis: A generational curse rooted in Hindu mythology haunts the descendants of an 1800s king who invoked Tavvai, the goddess of misfortune. Centuries later, his heirs are still paying the price — and searching for a way out.
picks.why_watch: Indian mythology meets horror is an underexplored genre — this one dives deep into generational karma.

picks.title: Super Subbu
picks.synopsis: Sundeep Kishan plays a sheltered young man whose overprotective schoolteacher father kept him away from all romantic experiences. The irony? He lands a job teaching sex education to adults in a remote village, colliding with rural life in ways he never imagined.
picks.why_watch: Telugu comedy with a premise so absurd it might just work — think culture clash meets coming-of-age, but backwards.

picks.title: Isakapatnam
picks.synopsis: Set in the 1990s in a fictional port town ruled by a powerful patriarch played by Samuthirakani, this seven-episode Telugu thriller follows his own daughter Bharati (Aishwarya Rajesh) as she rises to challenge his iron grip on the region.
picks.why_watch: Samuthirakani and Aishwarya Rajesh in a father-daughter power struggle — the 90s port-town setting is a bonus.

picks.title: Mollywood Times
picks.synopsis: Naslen plays an aspiring filmmaker inspired by M. Night Shyamalan, determined to make his debut feature. Part of director Abhinav Sunder Nayak's Success Trilogy following Mukundan Unni Associates, this satirical look at the Malayalam film industry blends dark humour with sharp commentary.
picks.why_watch: If you loved Mukundan Unni Associates, this is the spiritual sequel — same director, same savage industry satire.

picks.title: Muthassi
picks.synopsis: A mythological horror thriller set on the Kerala-Karnataka border. When Leela marries into a family whose ancestral home is steeped in superstition and supernatural activity, the birth of their first child triggers a chain of terrifying events rooted in generations of dark history.
picks.why_watch: Kerala folklore horror with a generational curse — ZEE5 has been quietly building a solid Malayalam horror slate.

picks.title: Enola Holmes 3
picks.synopsis: Millie Bobby Brown returns as Sherlock's brilliant younger sister, now heading to Malta for her wedding to Tewkesbury. But when Sherlock is kidnapped, Enola must choose between her new life and the case of a lifetime. From the director of Adolescence.
picks.why_watch: The Adolescence director takes over the franchise, and the Malta setting looks gorgeous — easily Netflix's biggest drop this week.

picks.title: Elle
picks.synopsis: Set in 1995, six years before Legally Blonde, this prequel follows teenage Elle Woods after she relocates from LA to Seattle when her father takes a new job. It traces the challenges and experiences that shaped the Elle we know and love.
picks.why_watch: If you grew up with Legally Blonde, seeing teenage Elle's origin story is irresistible nostalgia done right.

picks.title: Silo Season 3
picks.synopsis: Rebecca Ferguson's dystopian masterpiece returns with a 100% Rotten Tomatoes score. After the Season 2 rebellion, Juliette deals with memory loss while a parallel 'Before Times' storyline reveals the chilling origins of the silo. Colin Hanks and Jessica Brown Findlay join the cast.
picks.why_watch: 100% on Rotten Tomatoes, each season better than the last — this is the best sci-fi show most people aren't watching yet.

picks.title: Dark Winds Season 4
picks.synopsis: The acclaimed Navajo Nation crime thriller returns. Based on Tony Hillerman's mystery novels, the series follows Navajo Tribal Police officers Joe Leaphorn and Jim Chee as they solve crimes on the vast reservation in 1970s Arizona and New Mexico.
picks.why_watch: One of the best crime thrillers on any platform — the Southwest landscape and Navajo perspective make it truly unique.
